title: Using Multiple Outcomes to Adjust Standard Errors for Spatial Correlation
summary_en: Empirical research where each unit is a place — county, region, country — has to grapple with the fact that economic outcomes spill across borders, breaking standard cluster-robust inference. Lindner, DellaVigna and co-authors propose using the cross-sectional correlation of *other* outcomes observed for the same units to estimate the dependence structure, and show that the resulting Thresholding Multiple Outcomes (TMO) correction can substantially reduce bias in standard errors. Re-running nine recent papers, they find the correction often changes statistical conclusions.
data_used: Methodological paper. Calibration uses U.S. county-level data on multiple economic outcomes; re-analysis applies the proposed correction to nine recent published studies.
policy_relevance: Relevant to any Hungarian researcher or impact-evaluation team working with sub-national data — járás, kistérség, NUTS-3 region — including programme evaluations done by KSH, MNB, or KRTK. The TMO method offers a practical way to get standard errors right for spatially dependent outcomes without imposing arbitrary cluster boundaries; should become part of the standard Hungarian regional-policy evaluation toolkit.
